#3153. GTA 6 Review: The Megayacht of Gaming Has Something for Nearly Everyone

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Over a decade in the making, GTA 6 is a colossal, polished game with a core love story about the American dream: doing enough crime to retire early.

The most anticipated game in recent history, Grand Theft Auto 6, lives up to the hype. Expansive, interactive and peppered with so much to do that it’s easy to sink scores of hours into the launch game — and who knows how much more will be added later on.

GTA 6 iterates on the grandness of its predecessor, and in the 13 years since GTA 5 stretched gamer expectations with a huge map of seemingly endless activities, developer Rockstar Games has figured out how to layer a lot of granular detail into its next canvas of crime and carnage.

Environments that were sketched out in the last game, such as stores and buildings, are detailed and explorable. Bystanders and police react more naturally to your presence and culpability — cops now have to see you escaping the crime scene to tag you as a suspect for pursuit. You can talk people down from fights. And the game’s titular transgression of stealing cars is more nuanced than ever.

The standard edition of GTA 6 is available on Amazon now for PS5 and Xbox Series X and S.

If you prefer, you can preorder your copy of GTA 6 from Walmart.

Granted, early versions of some of these advancements were explored in Rockstar’s interim game, 2018’s Red Dead Redemption 2, and the series iteratively progressed with all the updates that continue to this day for GTA Online, which was built out from GTA 5 to be an ever-evolving game-as-a-service. But they’ve been taken to the next level in GTA 6, leading to a world that feels more responsive to your presence and actions. With all its systems, map space and activities, it feels like the megayacht of gaming — a polished experience in all its corners, with some of the most detailed graphics you’ll find in gaming.

A lot of that rests on the shoulders of the game’s protagonists, lovers in crime Lucia and Jason, who operate radically differently from previous GTA point-of-view characters. Their romance (if players choose to pursue it) offers a whole new narrative and systematic view of a life outside the law, with collaborative and solo missions that paint a vivid picture of the playful, dangerous world of GTA. Outside story missions, casually driving around as a couple fills the dead air with conversation and the robberies with partnered backup, enriched by their growing relationship, lathering their activities with all the sweetness of a violent date night.

The couple’s story is a very lengthy affair — at 50 hours in, the game says I’ve completed roughly 70% of it — and is robust enough to justify the price of entry. It’s a compelling narrative about two people trying to build a future through a dangerous world by leaning deeper into the danger, but it’s also a showcase of the world Rockstar built. After the story is done, the game hands you the keys to explore it yourself however you’d like.

Rockstar declined to comment on whether GTA 6 will transition into the next version of GTA Online, but it feels like an inevitability. It’s hard to ignore the vast space, systems and mechanics that players only briefly dabble with while playing through the story. From fishing to treasure hunting in underwater shipwrecks to big game hunting to street racing, there’s a lot of low-stakes fodder to unwind with the game — and plenty of bank heists, chases and other random crimes to ratchet up the tension, too.

At launch, GTA 6 has a broad foundation of things to do that — I suspect — will increase over time. It’s layered with Rockstar’s signature puerile humor, and I’ll fess up to laughing at some of the frequent boner jokes and crass names (one sportscar brand is the “pfister”), but the occasional homophobia and transphobia is bizarrely out of time — the game’s mock-everything culture still feels rooted in the 2000s, aimed at people who loved the edginess of South Park in its heyday. More modern satire appears in bystander conversations that range into absurd caricatures of far-right anti-woke crusaders and rabid leftists, but given the game’s faux-Florida setting in the fictional state of Leonida (which includes the legendary Vice City), there’s far more of the former than the latter.

Thus, the world feels textured even for players just picking up the game to fool around. While there are sparse stretches of the map, little side stories unfold for those who notice and follow strange things afoot. But a massive part of the game’s appeal and heart lies in the ballad of two lovebirds, kept apart by immaturity and circumstance but brought together through crime and the skewed American dream at the center of every GTA: Pull off a big enough heist and the world is yours.

The game’s story opens from Jason’s perspective — a twentysomething guy, former military, quiet and gruff, drifting through life doing odd jobs for a small-time kingpin out in the sticks. A little drug-running and skirmishing with the local gangs keep him busy, working out and drinking beers on his deck, watching the sunset from GTA 6’s version of the Florida Keys.

All that changes when Lucia, who stole and then broke his heart, gets out of prison on early release and asks to crash with him during her parole. A tenuous second chance is complicated when she reconnects with a former cellmate who’s partnered with a rich hotshot dangling wealth in front of our fragile couple. This could be the ticket to a financial foundation to help them start anew. Then a job goes wrong, and the pair go on the run, restarting in a rural backwater as far from the clubs of Vice City as one can get.

This is where players decide how close they want Jason and Lucia to be. The game sets up the beginnings of their reconnection, but they can drift apart if players don’t choose to bring them closer. It’s all about the little things: Jason holding the door for Lucia, one of them buying clothes for the other at the vendor, or even just sidling close during morning coffee. Rockstar didn’t want to force players into this relationship — even if things fizzle, the pair will still go through the game as partners in crime, doing jobs together even if they sleep apart.

But players will value something if they have to work for it, Rob Nelson, head of development at Rockstar North, told me over a video call. He likened the couple’s relationship to how players embraced the honor system in RDR2, with more taking the high honor route than being a vicious criminal.

“When you can lose something, it’s more meaningful if you work to keep it,” Nelson said.

As Nelson explained, Rockstar came off of GTA 5’s story with its three protagonists wondering how to one-up it for the sequel, which started development soon after in 2015 but took until early 2019 to settle on GTA 6’s main pair. A romantic couple is indeed a step up from characters who come together for a job and split after, and Rockstar had to figure out how that’s different for lovers — they’re not going to end a job at 2 a.m. and part ways; they’re going home to go to bed, Nelson said.

The couple essentially have a run-on conversation that lasts through the story, piping up during long drives to chat about a recent mission or bring up something from their pasts. How much these topics are tailored to events and how much are randomly chosen feels cleverly obscured, coming off like the natural chatter between two people slowly figuring each other out. The sheer scale of the recorded dialogue dwarfs other games and becomes a feature among many, showcasing the titanic work Rockstar put into GTA 6.

It all adds up to a compelling narrative centered on two characters, carefully chiseled to embody the best and worst of Vice City, inspired by the real-life Bonnie and Clyde and by crime couples from films like True Romance and Natural Born Killers. GTA 6’s couple starts with a meet-cute over trying to steal the same car, and freshly out of prison, Lucia eggs on Jason to take bigger illegal jobs than the small-time gigs he’s coasted on. Even with an ankle monitor and picking up road trash on work duty, Lucia never seriously considers staying on the right side of the law. Jason is cautious about new opportunities, but eager not to lose Lucia again, and never considers going straight.

Nestled within their stories is a serious point about the futility of staying honest in a city and system that caters to the rich and punishes the desperate. A flashback shows Lucia juggling gig-economy rideshare driving and having her utilities shut off after failed payments, which is heartbreakingly real. But it’s a blip amid the overwhelming focus on a criminal romance, where the only escape from poverty is to steal big bills until finally retiring to a distant island beyond the consequences of your felonious lifestyle.

It’s not surprising — that’s the GTA fantasy, after all — but it’s telling which things Rockstar took great pains to update to modern tastes over the game’s decade-plus development (and what it left out). Smartphones are a huge part of the game’s social interactions, from texting and calling contacts to Instagram-like social media feeds to summoning cars through an app or hailing a ride. But notably absent are any gig economy services that have normalized atypical incomes — you can’t TaskRabbit or Uber your way to an honest living in GTA 6. Odd jobs come as under-the-table favors you do for the rich and powerful, frequently taking advantage of both protagonists’ gray morals.

Though it won’t give you the option of a legal living, GTA 6 leans into the injustice of the wealth gap, putting a few city blocks between gang-riddled run-down apartments and the high-rise clubs populated by ignorant rich assholes. The game gleefully showcases the hypocrisy of the privileged — one time, I rushed into a rural, well-off house where a wife espousing family values ushered me to help her dying husband… who was choking in a BDSM leather harness. Once freed, he tucked his tail back into his submissive role as a “liberal cuck” for their roleplay.

This kind of edginess-for-laughs is peppered around the game, and it’s hard not to feel the cynicism. I can de-escalate some situations, but a lot of the non-player characters you run into on the street are on a hair-trigger, eager to fight. You’ll overhear plenty of anti-immigrant screeds from random bystanders. Junkies try to break into your car if you have contraband in the trunk.

If GTA 5 was released in the waning Obama years with waning public optimism, GTA 6 launches halfway into Trump’s second term, where far-right government ICE deportations and street killings have polarized the nation beyond anything we’ve seen in decades. Yet when I asked how Rockstar had adjusted the game over its long development to suit this moment, Nelson said that Jason and Lucia’s story is a counterweight of optimism and care amid all the crime and societal disparity in the game.

“Choosing love is a bit of an act of rebellion against a narcissistic culture,” Nelson said. “The ideas of selfishness and selflessness put through this world is interesting to us, giving you goals other than just maxing out your bank account with supercars and properties.”

Evaluating a game with so much detail spread across a vast map area is difficult, as the polish can be mistaken for quality. When I parked in a narrow driveway, I noticed Jason has an entire animation for shimmying through a slim gap. There have to be a dozen sequences for ways he and Lucia can sidle up to each other for a quick peck or embrace, all optional. There must be a thousand or more buildings you can duck into to explore their interiors. And the amount of dialogue feels unfathomably colossal, all voiced with aplomb by talented actors.

Where other games have some, GTA 6 has more. It’s a little like asking whether a megayacht is enjoyable to commute to work. The simple answer is yes, GTA 6 is an incredible game. And yet, its scope can be distracting. Halfway through the story, I was zipping from destroying drug dens to stealing valuable cars for a collector to hunting big game in the rural hills — all good fun, but my attention easily peeled away from the main story and the couple’s attempt to secure their financial independence, retire early future. The prior chapter had ended in a gun battle as hired killers came for a dangerous MacGuffin in Jason and Lucia’s hands, but amid all the good, clean street crime, that danger had receded to the background.

The story’s punch is diluted by everything you can and probably will do, which feels like forgetting the taste of the prime rib after sampling everything else at a buffet. But at least all those activities are enjoyable and round out the criminal with the casual, including mini golf and mud races far from the dense urban core of Vice City. It’s like if Lego Island grew up to add larceny to its roster of fun things to do.

In grappling with the scale of the game, I repeatedly reach for simile — too many options make it harder to fully define GTA 6 and who it’s for, outside of saying there’s so much that its appeal spreads very wide. There’s not quite something for everyone, but it offers such a plethora of side activities that if one gets tiring, another will probably tide you over. This is what will most likely form the foundation of an eventual transition to GTA Online: A substantial stream of things to do on top of stacking cash. And given GTAO’s sustained success, the baseline version of GTA 6 will please all the heist junkies and freeform adventurers who’ve loved the series, even if they aren’t hooked by the well-crafted core story. All the looky-loos curious about the hype will find one of the most polished and visually gorgeous video games ever made.

GTA fans will notice a lot of small improvements that clean up logical inconsistencies. Witnesses have to notice you doing a crime to report it, and cops have to see you flee a crime scene to put out an all-points bulletin on your description, though you can lower your chances of being recognized by swapping outfits and respraying the color of your getaway ride.

Other new features add complexity to the game. Certain crimes are riskier until you get new tools and connections unlocked through the story, which let you steal cars with trackers and rob banks with countermeasures. Exercise and diet affect your health and physique, which you’ll need to maintain with regular workouts. You can steal guns and vehicles, but they won’t be saved unless you pay to buy or register them, respectively.

These sound tedious, but they’re little frictions that make living in the world of GTA 6 more intentional. Early in the game as Jason, I frequently found myself waking up in the morning, grabbing a cup of coffee and doing a workout to get my in-game day “started,” putting on the radio and feeding my snake or checking in with Lucia ambling around the kitchen. As the relationship between the two deepens, they can go to bed together, cuddled up and doomscrolling on their phones.

While I expect a million posts of “he just like me fr fr” to blanket social media as people wonder at the work Rockstar put in to replicate our (often terrible) habits, there’s still a lot I was delighted to discover that’s unique to the world they’ve made. Some of these are jokes taken to an extreme, like the intentionally pretentious game-within-a-game you can play, Tenebrae Lux — a black-and-white walking simulator by an in-universe auteur, Johannes Zuch, whose name flashes on the screen so many times that it feels like a wink toward Hideo Kojima and other famous game creators.

“We love auteurs — it’s not mocking, it’s celebrating,” Nelson said.

But my favorite things in any GTA game are the side stories you can chance upon that are scripted but feel emergent, exploring the bizarre nooks and crannies of the world. One night halfway through the game, I was casually driving around as Lucia when I saw a police chopper aiming a spotlight at the street — and found the cops in a standoff with a man in a fox suit.

I immediately discovered that, in the game’s fictional state of Leonida, being a furry (e.g., wearing a fur suit and expressing your “fursona”) is illegal, so I broke through the police blockade to liberate him. I met up with his fellow furries and spirited them away to a compound, during which I peeked over my shoulder to find them nuzzling each other. God bless you little oddballs bravely living your truth in the face of unjust laws.

Like its forebears, GTA 6 feels like two games — a core narrative about making a living through the underground in a rags-to-riches-to-rags-to-riches saga of a star-crossed couple, and a massive sandbox to do whatever you want. While going treasure hunting in offshore wrecks or making drug drop-offs from a plane dilutes the story’s tension, it also gives you a lot of opportunity to find the GTA you want to experience. After the story fades into memory, that’s what’ll stick around as the core of this game: the freedom to choose what you want to do, laws be damned.

Eventually, you’ll face that ultimate temptation to cause such havoc that you’ll trigger the game’s new, sixth star of police attention — one in which it feels like every cop in Leonida is coming after you, and it doesn’t stop until you’re arrested or put down, a countdown to how long Jason and Lucia can stick it to the law at maximum volume.

“I haven’t played six stars since we finalized it. I made it too long, so we made it harder,” Nelson said. “I’m curious to see what times people get!”

#3152. Apple could build its AI health chatbot from this study – how to enroll

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Apple is leaning into AI-powered health tools with the launch of its Apple Health AI Usage Study.

Apple is exploring how people use AI for their health, presumably to build its own AI health coach. On Sunday, it launched the Apple Health AI Usage Study, which could contribute to the next AI health experience Apple builds by measuring the quality of AI health responses, comprehension, and everyday health behaviors, according to a press release.

Apple is conducting the study in collaboration with OpenEvidence, a clinical AI platform widely used by healthcare professionals. The study examines the relationship between conversational AI tools, like chatbots, and the people who use them.

“Insights from this study will help advance the broader scientific conversation and ensure that as technology evolves, we continue building trusted tools that genuinely support people wherever they are on their health journey,” Sumbul Desai, M.D., Apple’s vice president of Health and Fitness, said in the press release.

Also: Apple Watch Series 12 review: Finally, the health tracker I’ve been waiting for

Participants are encouraged to share their HealthKit data and query the health app with questions. The study will also explore how AI tools can best prepare patients ahead of clinical visits. Apple will monitor the AI’s clarity and approachability when providing medical information, and each response or recommendation will be linked to peer-reviewed clinical citations. Responses could be unclear or incomplete, which is why Apple is rolling this out as a study to explore a responsibly designed AI health assistant.

Apple often launches studies for features it would like to develop in the future. For example, many of the hearing health features launched on the AirPods were a direct result of the findings from Apple’s Hearing Study.

Also: Athenahealth patients can ask Claude about their medical records now

The AI usage study comes on the heels of the revamped Health app’s debut, which launches officially next month. It also arrives amid a bevy of AI health coaches, popping up alongside companion health devices. Google launched its AI Health Coach in Google Health Premium last year, and Oura launched a proprietary AI model for women trained on medical standards and research from Oura’s in-house team of board-certified clinicians.

A growing number of Americans are relying on AI for medical advice. A recent survey from Pew Research Center found that 34% of US adults have talked with a chatbot for medical advice. As AI proliferates, that percentage will only increase.

“Patients and clinicians are both turning to AI, but the tools they use are being built and tested in separate worlds,” said Robert M. Wachter, M.D., UCSF’s professor and chair of the Department of Medicine, in the press release.

Apple and other tech companies are building for this new health normal, and the AI usage study indicates that Apple isn’t taking the responsibility lightly.

If you’re interested in participating in Apple’s study, it’s open to 200,000 eligible participants age 21 and older in the US. You’ll need a phone with Apple Intelligence enabled (the iPhone 15 Pro or later), running iOS 26 or later. You can download the study app to learn more and enroll.

#3151. Bitmine Just Posted a Staggering $6.3 Billion Loss on Its Ethereum Position. Here's What ETH Investors Need to Know.

Tom Lee’s Bitmine kept catching a falling knife over the past year.

10 stocks we like better than Bitmine Immersion Technologies ›

Bitmine (BMNR -1.26%), which originally mined Bitcoin (BTC -0.38%), started buying Ether (ETH +0.51%) on June 30, 2025. Tom Lee, the company's new chairman, led that initiative to accumulate 5% of Ether's entire supply and build its own Ethereum Treasury.

Today, Bitmine holds about 6,077,745 Ether tokens, valued at roughly $10.8 billion and accounting for 4.97% of Ether's 122.2 million tokens. Unfortunately, Ether's price has also declined nearly 30% since Bitmine's first purchase last June.

Bitmine posted a staggering net loss of $6.3 billion in fiscal 2026 (which ended on Aug. 31). Most of that loss can be attributed to its poorly timed Ether purchases, but its Bitcoins also lost value over the past year. Moreover, Bitmine has nearly reached its target of buying 5% of Ether's supply, so it can't simply buy more tokens to reduce its average purchase price.

That's why Bitmine's stock has declined nearly 50% over the past 12 months. Should Ether investors consider that pullback to be a bright red flag for the cryptocurrency's future?

Tom Lee's bullish stance on Ether attracted a lot of attention, since he told investors to buy Bitcoin back in 2017, when it was still trading at about $2,600. Today, it trades at $63,000.

Lee began telling investors to buy Ether in late 2024, when it was trading at about $3,400. But today, it trades at about $1,800.

Lee had expected several catalysts to drive Ether's price higher. He expected Ethereum -- as the world's largest developer-oriented blockchain -- to grow as more stablecoins were minted and more real-world assets (RWAs) were tokenized on its network. He also expected more AI agents to use Ethereum for identity verification and machine-to-machine payments.

However, several headwinds crushed Ether over the past year. The outbreak of the Iran war exacerbated inflation, prompting the Fed to raise its benchmark rates for the first time in three years in September. That pressure drove investors toward more conservative investments.

The CLARITY Act, which would have provided a clearer path forward for cryptocurrencies, also died in the Senate, and the Democratic sweep of the midterm elections could lead to tighter regulations for Ether and other altcoins. Therefore, Ether could remain under pressure unless interest rates decline and the government establishes clearer rules for cryptocurrencies.

That's bad news for Bitmine, which has nearly run out of room for fresh Ether purchases, but it isn't necessarily bad news for Ether investors who can look past the near-term challenges. The catalysts Lee mentioned could still drive Ether's price higher, but it could take a lot longer than expected in this challenging macro environment.

#3148. Oura’s new feature could help you kick jet lag – how to enable it

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Oura just launched a Jet Lag Plan to help you stay alert when you switch time zones, whether you're traveling for business or pleasure.

Oura developed a tool for its frequent-flying members that could help them stave off the worst of jet lag.

Ahead of the busy holiday travel season, on Tuesday, Oura announced Jet Lag Plan, a new feature designed to help travelers feel alert and energized after crossing several time zones.

Also: Oura Ring users may get in-app access to real doctors soon – what we know

Jet Lag Plan takes into account your travel itinerary, sleep patterns, and body responses to provide guidance for traveling members entering new time zones.

Jet lag happens when circadian rhythms are at odds with local time zones, but there are a few things people can do to adjust.

Oura factors in the direction of travel, how many time zones are crossed, individual light windows, and sleep timing.

Ring users will enter their flight details, including information like multi-stop trips, and also include the reason for the trip. Oura adjusts the Jet Lag Plan accordingly, and a business trip’s plan may differ in intensity from that of a vacation.

“Two people on the same flight can get different plans, because guidance reflects your itinerary, your typical sleep schedule, and your chronotype,” Oura writes in a blog post. The chronotype refers to Oura’s sleep chronotype, which categorizes users into six types (early morning, morning, early evening, and so on) based on their historical sleep activity.

After adding these details, Oura provides each user with timely guidance throughout their trip. This guidance could include recommendations on when to begin or end caffeine consumption or light exposure, and when to start preparing for sleep. The plan is designed for those crossing three or more time zones. Members can follow along with these recommendations by checking them off as they complete each one. Users can also talk to Oura’s Advisor in the event of flight or timing changes.

Jet Lag Plan is now available for Oura Members with Oura Ring Gen 3 or later.

Go to your home screen, tap the + and select Jet Lag Plan to get started. You can also tell Oura Advisor about a trip to initiate Jet Lag Plan. If the Oura app detects a time zone shift of 3 or more hours, Jet Lag Plan may appear as a push notification.

#3147. Disney Imagineers Have Built AI-Powered ‘Star Wars’ Alien Audio-Animatronics With AWS

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Semi-exclusive: Three original Anzellan characters with distinct personalities will interact with guests in Disney parks.

Disney is celebrating 75 years of its Imagineers, who have been amusing and delighting guests with audio-animatronic characters since talking parrots debuted in the Enchanted Tiki Room at Disneyland. But today, new robotic characters are being powered up with artificial intelligence.

In partnership with Amazon Web Services, AI has helped Walt Disney Imagineering create three new Anzellan animatronics that will live bring a Disney theme park retail space to life, presumably in Star Wars: Galaxy’s Edge.

Anzellans are a race of tiny humanoid creatures that repair droids and starships in the Star Wars universe. They include Babu Frik in Star Wars: Episode IX — The Rise of Skywalker and the droidsmiths introduced in season 3 of The Mandalorian. The droidsmiths take on larger roles in The Mandalorian and Grogu, helping Baby Yoda rescue Din Djarin from the Hutts.

The new Anzellan animatronics built by Disney Imagineers use AWS cloud and AI capabilities in order to “understand the scene around them,” Kyle Laughlin, SVP of Walt Disney Imagineering R&D and Technology and Engineering, tells me.

“If you imagine walking into an experiential retail store, you now will be greeted not by a pre-scripted animation or interaction, but a totally personalized experience where each of these Anzellans [has] their own personalities,” Laughlin says, adding that they’ll be attuned to how many people are nearby and whether they’re children or adults.

The animatronic aliens will be able to interact with guests, right down to commenting on people who are wearing a birthday button or even a certain Star Wars T-shirt. Speaking with these animatronics will give guests the same experience they would have when meeting a character walking around the park, Laughlin adds. They also play off each other and react to what each other are doing, with no one controlling them behind the scenes.

The three audio-animatronic prototypes, which will make their first appearance during AWS re:Invent in Las Vegas on Nov. 30 before moving into one of the Disney Parks, are named Vilo Vele, Kado Bre’a and Jibu Bre’a.

They’re original characters created just for this project in partnership with Lucasfilm and the filmmakers, and they all have their own personalities devised by the Imagineers. Vilo is the boss, Kado is the droidsmith mechanic who wants to be the center of attention and Jibu, though Kado’s twin, is the shy one. The animatronics speak a mix of English (or Galactic Basic in-universe) and Anzellan, as they do in the Star Wars movies and TV series, and have hundreds of thousands of prerecorded lines of dialogue to draw from when talking to guests and each other.

Samira Panah Bakhtiar, AWS general manager of Telco, Media & Entertainment, Games, Advertising and Sports, tells me this is “one of the most delightful examples” of physical AI.

“When you talk about physical AI, it’s AI that perceives, it reasons and it acts in the real world,” she says. “It’s not just AI on a screen.”

Bakhtiar says Disney was able to use both AWS cloud computing and AI tools to “get from idea to implementation several magnitudes faster than they would have otherwise,” with Laughlin specifying it took “mere months.”

AWS staff used a coding agent called Kiro that built their creative briefs into software, which was then reviewed and approved by humans. Imagineers also used the Amazon Bedrock fully managed AI service, which allows them to choose between all the biggest AI models, including those from OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta.

“We’re providing Amazon Bedrock to the Imagineering team to be able to leverage the right models that they need at the right time to be able to really enhance those character experiences,” Bakhtiar tells me. “From multimodal models that focus on voice to world models, to large language models. The point is that they are able to get the right tool at the right time and then do so in a way that’s secure, resilient, performant and globally available.”

Bakhtiar says AWS is continuing to work with Disney, though the next project is under wraps.

“The future of entertainment is going to be highly personalized,” she says. “It’s going to be multidimensional, and it’s going to be more interactive than ever. And I think this is an incredible example of that coming to life.”

Disney had previously teamed up with Nvidia on robotics and AI to bring a robot version of fan-favorite Frozen character Olaf to life so he can wander around Disneyland Paris and Hong Kong Disneyland, and is also now exploring robots paired with AI that could guide guests throughout Disneyland parking lots.

“You can imagine an entire franchise of characters working and interacting with one another,” says Laughlin. “We’ve done a number of things in the Star Wars universe. We’re just getting started in Frozen, and we have a wealth of IP that we can mine to bring those characters to our guests as fast as possible.”

Correction, 3:48 p.m. ET: The original version of this story incorrectly stated who used the Kiro coding agent to build the software. It was staff from AWS.

#3144. Own 2 Android phones? Google may let you switch service fast – like iPhone Handoff

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Mobile OS > Android

If Android Fast Switch works like iPhone Handoff, one eSIM can be quickly switched between two phones.

In iOS 27, Apple announced iPhone Handoff, a networking feature that allows users to switch cell service between two eSIM-enabled iPhones. Text strings in Google’s SIM Manager app suggest the company is preparing a similar feature for compatible Android phones, according to Android Authority.

Code strings include “Use a SIM on two phones,” and note that the feature will be called Fast Switch. Little information is currently available about the feature’s limitations, including which phones or mobile carriers may not be compatible.

Also: Why your USB-C cables look alike, but work differently – and how to tell them apart

On Apple’s side, any iPhone in the US running iOS 27 with a T-Mobile or Verizon-provided eSIM can use iPhone Handoff. AT&T does not currently support iPhone Handoff.

However, the code strings uncovered by Android Authority show that Android’s Fast Switch will work similarly to iPhone Handoff, in that users must be signed in to both devices under the same Google account for the feature to work.

Strings in Google’s SIM Manager app also point to no sharing between two users, so this feature isn’t a way to circumvent carrier fees by adding service to someone else’s phone for the price of one.

If Fast Switch works anything like iPhone Handoff, which it appears it will, one eSIM can be switched between two phones. So, calls, messages, location services, and other information synced to your Apple ID can remain consistent between two devices.

Also: 5 hidden iOS 27 features that make older iPhones better

Some third-party apps, like banking, communications, or social media, may also remain consistent across the two phones, depending on the app’s syncing behavior.

Features like Apple’s iPhone Handoff and Google’s Fast Switch are ideal for people who regularly use two phones. Business owners and digital creators may want one phone strictly for business purposes and the other for personal use.

Also: Google Wallet turns your Android phone into a digital house key

In that case, one person can keep up with two phones without paying for two phone service lines through their carrier. Still, users will incur a fee, as T-Mobile charges $5/month for iPhone Handoff, while Verizon charges $10/month.

#3143. Which Laptops Last the Longest? Check Out the Laptops I’ve Tested With the Best Battery Life

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

As part of our video series Holiday Office Hours From the Labs, I share laptop recommendations and explain why battery life surged in 2026.

I can almost guarantee that your next laptop will run longer on battery power than whatever you’re currently using. We’ve seen a huge leap in laptop battery life in recent years, to the point where getting 20 or more hours on a single charge isn’t uncommon. This year alone, the average battery life of the laptops we’ve tested at CNET has increased by more than five hours. And it’s nearly doubled since the start of the decade.

With many of today’s laptops, you can leave the charger at home for days at a time. The longest-lasting laptop I tested this year lasted more than 34 hours!

This increase in battery life is one of the biggest stories in laptops this year. In the laptop episode of our video series Holiday Office Hours From the Labs, I explain what’s behind this surge in battery life and highlight some of the laptops that lasted the longest in testing.

Plus, my colleagues Kyle Kucharski from ZDNET and Joe Osborne from PCMag share their own holiday laptop picks. Kyle looks at Apple’s entry-level MacBook Neo and its imitators, and Joe breaks down what to look for in a budget gaming laptop.

Unlike raw performance, where the more you spend, the more you get, lengthy battery life can be found just as easily in a budget laptop as in an expensive, high-end powerhouse. And, in fact, less powerful components and lower screen resolutions can give cheaper laptops an edge in battery life.

The biggest factor behind longer battery life in laptops is the advancement in mobile processors. They’ve become much more power efficient, and in the case of Apple’s and Qualcomm’s chips, they’re based on an architecture other than the traditional x86 instruction set that’s been at the heart of Intel processors since the dawn of the PC era.

Apple’s run of battery-life winners started when it shifted from Intel processors to its own M-series chips. Apple’s M-series processors are based on the Arm architecture, a power-efficient chip architecture found in phones and tablets. Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X-series processors are also Arm-based, and they can be found in the two longest-running laptops we’ve tested: the HP OmniBook 3 16 and OmniBook 5 14. The OmniBook 3 16’s record-setting battery performance earned it a CNET Lab Award for longest battery life.

Intel has made huge strides in processor efficiency with its last two generations of chips: the Core Ultra 200 series developed under the name Lunar Lake, and the Core Ultra 300 series, also known as Panther Lake. Last year, the Lenovo Yoga 9i 2-in-1 Aura Edition became the first Intel laptop to last longer than a day, running for 25 hours, 45 minutes in testing. It’s still the longest-running Intel laptop we’ve tested, but the MSI Prestige 14 Flip AI Plus with Intel’s next-gen Core Ultra X7 358H processor came close with a time of 25 hours, 18 minutes.

Read more: Laptops With the Best Battery Life

Whether Arm or x86, there are two more reasons behind greater processor efficiency and longer laptop battery life. For one, the size of a processor shrinks with every generation. The smaller a processor is and the more tightly packed its components are, the less power is required to flip its tinier transistors on and off. For another, today’s mobile processors feature more flexible designs with a mix of performance and efficiency cores. A processor engages its higher-performance cores only when needed, using the efficiency cores for as many general, everyday tasks as possible, so your laptop stays cool and quiet and runs longer.

For more, you can read my Labs exclusive on the huge increase in laptop battery life this year and check out the video above for my holiday laptop picks and those from my colleagues.

#3142. UK court rules Apple can share the top secret order everyone already knew

The Investigatory Powers Tribunal – essentially a British court that deals with complaints about state surveillance – has ruled that Apple is allowed to reveal a secret order it received from the UK government.

Apple had already found a clever way to alert British customers to the classified order without breaking the law, but it can now confirm what we all already knew, and talk openly about the issue …

In 2025, the British government ordered Apple to create a backdoor to allow access by security services and law enforcement. Even worse, the order was issued under legislation that prohibits companies from revealing that they have received this demand.

This would have meant that British customers who enabled ADP would think that their data was safe when in fact it wasn’t. As we’ve said many times before, any backdoor created for use by the good guys is vulnerable to discovery and exploitation by the bad guys.

“Apple can no longer offer Advanced Data Protection (ADP) in the United Kingdom to new users and current UK users will eventually need to disable this security feature. ADP protects iCloud data with end-to-end encryption, which means the data can only be decrypted by the user who owns it, and only on their trusted devices. We are gravely disappointed that the protections provided by ADP will not be available to our customers in the UK […] As we have said many times before, we have never built a backdoor or master key to any of our products or services and we never will.”

Tell me you’ve been ordered to create a backdoor to ADP without telling me you’ve been ordered to create a backdoor to ADP …

The UK government must admit that it issued a secret order to Apple to allow it access to encrypted customer data, a court has ruled […] The Home Office has “not established that it would be damaging to national security” to reveal that Apple had received a “technical capability notice” (TCN), the tribunal said. The ruling means that […] “much” of Apple and the non-profits’ legal challenge can now take place in open court.

One of the great ironies is that most people had never heard of ADP until the government effectively made it headline news in the tech press three years after it launched – a classic example of the Streisand Effect.

This ruling is a win both for transparency and commonsense. To be clear, the actual requirement for a backdoor remains in place, but this can now be challenged in open court.

#3141. Apple reveals daily limits on your Siri AI use – here’s how much you’ll have to pay

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

The more you pay for an iCloud+ plan, the more you’ll be able to use Siri AI and Apple Intelligence for advanced server-side tasks.

Have you been using the new Siri AI? If so, how much? I’ve been turning to it a lot since the release of iOS 27. Well, how we use it — and how often — will soon depend on how much we pay for an iCloud+ plan.

Also: 5 apps I need Siri AI to work with now that it’s open to third-party developers

Apple hasn’t been shy about stating that the use of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence for specific tasks would face daily access limits. Increased limits would be granted based on your iCloud+ subscription. Now the company has revealed how much it will cost you and when the limits will begin.

“Starting with the 2027 software releases, Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features are available for free for users with a supported device set to a supported language,” Apple said on a support page updated November 16. “Some features rely on powerful server models and have limits where increased access is available with eligible iCloud+ plans, starting with the 27.3 release.”

iOS 27.3 is expected to launch in early December, so that’s when the daily usage limits will kick in.

At that point, people with no paid iCloud+ plan and even those with the $0.99-per-month 50 GB plan will be the most limited, with Apple saying only that they’ll face a “Standard Device Limit.”

What is a standard limit? That depends not just on how many times you tap into Siri per day but on what tasks you assign it. Basic Siri commands, such as setting timers and alarms or sending standard text messages, will remain free and unlimited.

Also: Ready for a Siri AI agent? Apple under pressure to upgrade its assistant faster

Advanced Siri and Apple Intelligence tasks will bump into the usage limits. These include the following, according to Apple:

One positive here is that the limits are per device not per account. That means you can use Siri AI and Apple Intelligence with the same account across your iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, and Vision Pro without fear of chewing up too much of your quota.

This all sounds like a way for Apple to steer people to more expensive iCloud+ accounts. But the limits are in place for a key reason. Basic commands are processed on your device, so they don’t require the use of Apple servers. More advanced tasks are processed using server-side AI models, which can feel the strain if too many people access them all at once.

Also: What you’ll pay for AI agents will be wildly variable and unpredictable

How will you know if you use up your daily allotment and what happens then? You’ll receive a notification if you hit your limit for a particular feature category. At that point, you can still give Siri basic tasks to perform. But advanced ones will be paused until your limit resets the next day. Otherwise, Apple is undoubtedly hoping that people who continually run into limits will upgrade to a pricier iCloud+ plan.

The company reached a global market utilization of 93% for modern jack-ups and anticipates that full-year 2027 performance will align with 2026 levels. Operator: Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the Borr Drilling Limited Q3 2026 results presentation conference call and webcast. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speaker's presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during the session, please press star one on your telephone. You will then hear an automated message advising your hand is raised. To withdraw your question, please press star one again. Please also note that today's conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the conference over to your speaker, Mr. Bruno Morand, CEO. Please go ahead, sir.

Bruno Morand: Good morning, and thank you for participating in Borr Drilling third quarter earnings call. I am Bruno Morand, and with me here today is Magnus Vaaler, our Chief Financial Officer. I would like to remind all participants that certain statements made on this call are forward-looking and involve risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those projected in these statements. For further details, please refer to our latest public filings. Before I turn to the quarter, I want to speak about the Prospector 5 incident. On October 24, the Prospector 5 suffered a catastrophic loss of stability during pre-loading operations and subsequently sunk offshore Gabon while working for our customer, BW Energy.

At the time of the incident, 115 people were on board, and 110 were brought safely ashore to Port Gentil. Sadly, four people lost their lives, and one person remains unaccounted for. The search and rescue efforts are still ongoing. On behalf of Borr Drilling, I extend our deepest sympathy to the families, friends, and colleagues of those individuals who lost their lives and to the family still waiting for news. In the days after the incident, I traveled to Gabon to meet the crews, the families of those affected, and the team leading the emergency response efforts. The commitment and professionalism of individuals involved in the response efforts has been both touching and reassuring.

We are very grateful to each and every person supporting these efforts, the government of Gabon, BW Energy, and the broader offshore community for the extraordinary cooperation and support they have provided us during this difficult time. We have engaged DNV, a globally recognized classification society, to conduct an independent investigation to determine the root cause of the incident. Early information from the site pointed to a possible punch-through event. Since then, we have reviewed additional information as it became available to us, including ROV survey data, video footage from BW Energy. That review has not confirmed a punch-through event, and the cause has not yet been established. The Prospector 5 has since been declared a total loss.

The rig insured value is $200 million, with insurance payment date set for November 24th, 2026. Additionally, we carry comprehensive third-party liability insurance, which includes coverage related to wreck removal and pollution. Together with BW Energy, we are evaluating preliminary solutions to enable a safe and efficient resumption of drilling activities at MaBoMo platform in the near term. This has been a tragic event for our company, and our priority remains supporting the affected families and everyone impacted. With that in mind, I will now turn the call to a quarterly update. Our third quarter 2026 operations result in technical utilization of 98% and economic utilization of 97.3%.

Revenues for the period were $263.1 million, with an average of 22.9 operating rigs. Third quarter adjusted EBITDA was $78.9 million, consistent with our expectations. Magnus will provide further details later. We currently anticipate Q4 adjusted EBITDA performance to be broadly in line with Q3, despite the Prospector 5 impact. In September, as previously announced, we streamlined our operation in Mexico by divesting our interest in the Perfomex joint ventures. Together with our recent acquisition of five premium units from Fontis, this rationalization of Perfomex strengthened our local alignment and creates a more efficient structure, positions us for potential growth and deployment of further rigs as demand develops in Mexico.

On the contracting front, since our last quarterly report, we have secured nine new commitments in key geographies outside of the Middle East. These include an award to deploy the previously idle rig, Hild, offshore Nigeria, strengthening our presence in this growing market. These commitments added approximately $269 million in backlog and represents more than 1,950 days of additional firm work, bringing our coverage for 2026 and 2027 to 79% and 52%, respectively. We are also seeing encouraging signs of shallow water activity, with increasing number of opportunities in Southeast Asia and West Africa in particular.

Despite persistent disruptions in the Middle East, recent contract developments continue to strengthen market utilization for modern jack-ups, which now stands at 93% compared to around 90% nine months ago. This is already a tight market and provides a strong starting point for pricing to appreciate as incremental demand comes through. Based on the current forward coverage, we anticipate full year 2027 adjusted EBITDA to be broadly in line with full year 2026, with expectations for Q1 2027 to be sequentially lower and a stronger ramp-up in Q4. These reflect the timing of the market recovery against our fleet availability, with a higher number of rigs open in the first half of the year.

That being said, we remain positive on the outlook for the jack-ups, and the same availability should position to capture upside as demand materializes through 2027. The company's strong liquidity position provides the financial flexibility to capitalize on opportunities as the market recovers. For now, our near-term priority remains maximizing fleet utilization while maintaining a disciplined approach to long-term commitments to create sustainable shareholder value. I will walk you through the market and the fleet in more detail later in the call, but now I will hand the call to Magnus to discuss the third quarter financial results.

Magnus Vaaler: Thank you, Bruno. I will now go into some details on the financials of the third quarter. Total operating revenues for Q3 were $263.1 million, an increase of $30.8 million, or 13%, compared to Q2. Total operating revenues consisted of $216.8 million in day rate revenue, $36.4 million in variable charter revenue, and $9.9 million in management contract revenue. The decrease was primarily due to a $10.8 million reduction in the provision of credit losses compared to the prior quarter.

This $10.8 million decrease is offset by higher operating costs due to more rigs operating in the quarter and in higher-cost jurisdictions such as West Africa and the U.S., in addition to higher insurance costs in the Middle East. Loss from equity method investments for Q3 was $6.7 million, an increase in loss of $6.4 million compared to Q2, primarily due to the recognition of $4.7 million of losses attributable to our new joint venture. Total financial expenses net were $56.3 million, a decrease of $180.2 million compared to Q2. The decrease was primarily due to the $176.3 million loss on extinguishment of debt recognized in the prior quarter in connection with our refinancing.

Additionally, we had $3.7 million reduction in interest expense resulting from lower interest rates on the new debt. Net loss for Q3 was $38.7 million, a decrease in loss of $202.7 million compared to Q2. Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 was $78.9 million, an increase of $35.1 million, or 80%, compared to Q2. Net cash provided by operating activities for Q3 was $31.6 million, which includes $6.3 million of income taxes paid. Net cash used in investing activities for Q3 was $52.7 million. This consisted of $40.9 million of loans provided to our joint venture, BC Ventures, including the $25 million related to our share of the cash consideration for the Fontis acquisition. In addition, we had $11.8 million of additions to jack-up drilling rigs, primarily long-term maintenance costs and capital additions for drilling equipment. Our liquidity position provides a strong foundation for the company and the financial flexibility to capitalize on opportunities as the market recovers. Changing topics to a few words on the financial aspects of the Prospector 5 incident.

The rig has been declared a total loss, which resulted in the automatic termination of the drilling contract with BW Energy on October 24th. The remaining firm term backlog under that contract was approximately $45 million. The net book value of the rig was approximately $95 million at the end of Q3. The company is continuing to evaluate the full consequences of the incident, including the resulting write-off of the rig, potential insurance recoveries, potential losses, contractual impacts, legal matters, or claims that may arise, and other related matters.
