#3082. Grand Theft Auto 6 Is Out. Here’s How to Make Room on Your Console

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

You can make space on your console for GTA 6 a few different ways.

The wait is over. Grand Theft Auto 6 is out, and it is massive. The game is 212 GB, which means it takes up about half of the storage space on my Xbox Series S. The company announced that GTA 6 is available to stream via Xbox Cloud Gaming without downloading it to your console. However, cloud streaming GTA 6 might affect the game’s performance and relies heavily on a strong internet connection. To avoid those issues, I plan on downloading the game.

If you’re like me and are excited to play GTA 6 but don’t have much storage space, you have a few options: delete games, upgrade your console’s hard drive and streaming the game. Here’s what you should know about these options.

The simplest and cheapest way to free up space on your console for Grand Theft Auto 6 is to delete files and other games, which is what I’ll be doing. Uninstalling games is a good choice for folks who plan on spending a lot of time with GTA 6 and don’t intend to juggle different games. Rob Nelson, who oversees Rockstar North with Aaron Garbut, told The New York Times that he had an 80-hour playthrough of the game in February, so you can easily stay immersed in Grand Theft Auto’s state of Leonida.

You may not need to delete much – uninstalling a game like Call of Duty alone could free up nearly 315 GB, giving you enough digital storage for GTA 6. Since deleting files is almost instantaneous, you can quickly reclaim hard drive space. Because you don’t need to buy additional storage, you’ll also save a lot of money – storage prices are through the roof at the moment.

Ultimately, deleting games is a great option if you don’t want to spend any additional money or you don’t mind redownloading games later.

If you plan on hopping between GTA 6 and other games, or you don’t want to delete many of your downloaded titles, you can upgrade your console’s storage. Buying storage is more expensive than deleting files from your console, but benefit from being able to seamlessly hop between Grand Theft Auto 6 and Call of Duty or Madden.

You can use internal or external storage for your console, but you might have to move files between your internal and external storage to launch games. An internal hard drive lets you seamlessly play games. Xbox consoles rely on proprietary expansion cards from Seagate or SanDisk that plug into your console for additional storage. The PlayStation 5 uses M.2 solid-state drives, which are installed alongside the PS5’s built-in storage, and CNET’s David Carnoy recommends the Lexar NM 790 as a fast SSD with a straightforward installation process.

There shouldn’t be any performance, quality or load-time differences between running games from installed storage expansion devices versus your console’s internal storage. Both expansion cards and SSDs can be expensive, especially when compared with deleting games.

You could also use an external hard drive to expand your storage, which can be cheaper than buying expansion cards and internal SSD upgrades – you may even have a compatible USB external drive sitting around that you can use. However, there are caveats around what games can and can’t be played directly from external HDDs.

For Xbox consoles, some older Xbox, Xbox 360 and Xbox One titles can be stored and played from external HDDs. But games optimized for Series X/S consoles can only be stored on HDDs and must be moved back to your internal drive to play. Similarly, the PlayStation 5 only lets you store PS5 games on external HDDs, while you can store and run PS4 games from external drives.

Therefore, using an external HDD requires playing digital musical chairs, moving current-gen games back and forth between your external hard drive and internal console storage in order to play them. The LaCie Rugged SSD4 earned a CNET Editors’ Choice Award and could be a good option. If its price tag scares you, the Western Digital P10 offers more storage at a more economical price point.

Rockstar announced that GTA 6 is available to stream on the Xbox consoles – no download required – via Xbox Cloud Gaming, with some quality and time limitations. You’ll need to buy either an Xbox Game Pass plan or Cloud Gaming hours. Folks who don’t want to delete games or upgrade their console storage can stream GTA 6, but you’ll need an Xbox One or Series X/S console, you won’t get the highest visual quality and you will have to pay for more playtime hours if they run out. Streaming GTA 6 could help budget-conscious gamers who don’t want to upgrade from Xbox One consoles or who don’t have the allotted storage space on their devices.

Normally, you can stream many games on PCs, mobile devices and TVs or streaming devices using Xbox Cloud Gaming or Game Pass, but Grand Theft Auto 6 is limited to the Xbox One, Series S and Series X. Additionally, GTA 6 streaming quality is capped at Series S graphical settings. So if you have a Series X, consider deleting games or upgrading your storage to run the game locally with better graphics.

While you’ll need to install the full game on your console first, remote play for Xbox and PlayStation consoles lets you stream GTA 6 to other devices, like your phone, tablet, streaming device or TV.

If you’re willing to pay a little more for the convenience of having multiple games ready to play at a moment’s notice, Xbox expansion cards or an internal SSD for a PS5 are your best options. If you want a cheaper option and don’t mind moving game files around, an external hard drive could be for you. If you have Xbox Game Pass or Xbox Cloud Gaming, you could stream the game to your console without needing more storage space. However, the cheapest option is to delete games from your internal storage and redownload them later, which can be time-consuming.

I chose the cheapest option and deleted a few games from my Xbox. I’m not planning on leaving GTA 6 any time soon.

#3080. The Flipper One is more than a Zero 2.0 – it’s a $399 Linux computer with a $13M Kickstarter

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Linux

Backers are going big on the $759 Ultimate Bundle, but Flipper warns that rising RAM prices could affect production.

The Flipper One crowdfunding campaign has broken the $13-million mark, smashing the funding raised for previous Flipper devices and demonstrating strong interest in the successor to the Flipper Zero. The $399 Flipper One is a pocket Linux computer focused on networking, with delivery estimated for July 2027. But it isn’t simply an updated version of the Flipper Zero. It’s a very different animal and a much more serious bit of kit.

The thing that made the Flipper Zero so popular was how easy it was to use. You could fire it up and turn the volume down on the TV at your parents’ place, see the radio waves coming from your car’s key fob, and copy hotel room key cards.

Also: The Flipper One may be the ultimate Linux PC for hackers in 2026 – and I’m excited

It could do a lot, there wasn’t a steep learning curve, and you didn’t need to buy anything else. Did the fake videos on TikTok from people claiming they could change the prices at gas stations (I wish!) or start cars remotely help make the Zero more popular?

Unfortunately, yes. But what made it successful was that it packed a lot of power into a package that was small, fun, affordable, and easy to use.

If the Flipper Zero, with its NFC, RFID, sub-GHz, and IR, was kindergarten, the Flipper One is a college degree: a pocket Linux computer focused on networking.

This is reflected in the price. You can pick up a Zero for $169, while the Flipper One is $399.

What this buys you is the Flipper One base computer with a 256 × 144 grayscale LCD, Rockchip RK3576 8-core ARM SoC with NPU, a low-power MCU for handling the LCD and user interface, 8GB of LPDDR5 RAM, 64GB of UFS 2.2 storage, and a microSD slot.

If that $399 feels like a lot, it’s worth keeping in mind that, according to Flipper, the price only covers production costs and that the RAM and UFS storage account for at least half of the total hardware cost.

If you think this is a lot, you could spend a lot more. Adding a LoRa, SDR, or 5G module will push the total up a lot higher. And if you want all three modules, you’re looking at $759 for the Flipper One Ultimate Bundle.

Also: The Flipper One is the Linux cyberdeck I wish my Raspberry Pi could be

The reception has been strong enough that pledges have flown past the $300,000 goal that Flipper initially set, with over 24,000 backers pledging over $13 million. Close to 5,300 backers have gone for the Ultimate Bundle, compared to just over 4,300 choosing the bare Flipper One.

This suggests that backers really want the radio capabilities that this new platform offers.

If you want one, this crowdfunding run is a good time to get one because it’s a Kickstarter Special slashing 25% off an estimated retail price of $550.

The response over on Reddit has been a little more subdued, with some being taken aback by the price of the Zero’s bigger sibling.

Also: 7 useful things I can do with my Flipper Zero – as someone who’s used it for years

As someone who homebrews a lot of electronics, I’m going to say that the price is justified, and this project goes far beyond something you could put together with a Raspberry Pi and some code.

The Flipper One campaign runs until Dec. 17, 2026, with delivery estimated for July 2027.

Keep in mind that this is a Kickstarter pledge, not a purchase, and that rewards aren’t guaranteed. Flipper also says on the Kickstarter page that component shortages are the biggest risk to the project and that they “could cause significant delays to production and delivery.” It also says that if RAM prices continue to rise, it cannot “rule out adjusting some product specifications, including reducing the amount of RAM.”

Also: Is the Flipper Zero the best multi-tool for hacking?

And the good news here is that I’ve seen several analysts predicting that RAM prices will begin to go down in 2027 as demand eases off.

#3079. Black Friday Sales Are Days Away, but Most US Adults Aren’t Waiting, CNET Finds

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Over one-third have already started holiday shopping, but November's sales could yield big savings.

Even though early holiday sales started months ago, shopping your wish lists during Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales may be worth the wait if you’re one of the few planning to shop November sales. It’s the time to save money on most tech devices. But holiday shopping could look different for US adults juggling smaller budgets and shopping frustrations.

CNET’s annual holiday shopping survey shows that 27% of US adults plan to start holiday shopping in November and 17% plan to shop during sales. However, US adults will be juggling a smaller tech budget of $808. That’s $123 less than CNET’s survey findings last year.

Finding savings is paramount to staying within your price range this year, but how can you spot a good deal when nearly every retailer is having a sale? CNET experts weighed in on US adults’ holiday shopping plans and shared expert advice to score the best Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals on must-haves.

CNET found that 27% will plan or start their holiday shopping this month, with 17% of November shoppers planning to shop holiday sales, like Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

The big question is whether the sales are worthwhile. CNET’s director of commerce content, Russell Holly, says it comes down to when you find a deal on a must-have item.

“The best time to buy is the moment you see something you want on an actual discount, because increased prices can come at any time,” Holly said.

Holly says even steep discounts aren’t lowering prices as much as before, but the right deals may make you reconsider. You just have to know where and when to shop for tech devices.

For example, Black Friday is usually the best time to buy electronics, including TVs and robot vacuums, with the biggest deals lasting from Black Friday to Cyber Monday.

CNET’s senior laptops editor, Matt Elliott, says if you’re planning to buy a new laptop during holiday sales, look for discounts at Amazon, Best Buy and vendor sites like Dell, HP and Lenovo.

“These retailers and companies are constantly rotating discounts on laptops, and these sales can save you hundreds of dollars. So, it’s worth tracking the price of a laptop you want and buying it when it dips,” said Elliott.

Black Friday and Cyber Monday are also a good time to buy the latest wearables, said CNET’s wearable expert, Vanessa Hand Orellana.

“For Black Friday, all the heavy wearable hitters tend to go on sale: Google, Samsung, Oura, Garmin and Apple,” said Orellana. However, if you don’t need the latest tech, you can find some of the best deals on last year’s tech at third-party retailers, like Best Buy and Walmart. And many of the previous-gen models share the same features as the newest ones, said Orellana.

CNET’s deals team spends hours making sure sales are legitimate — not just a fake price drop. And in the coming weeks, they’ll track deals on devices like laptops, headphones, wearable devices and smart home gadgets, plus alternatives to more costly tech, to help you determine what’s worth buying now or later.

You can also check an item’s price history to see if you’re getting the best deal by using price trackers like CamelCamelCamel and comparing prices across retailers before buying. But as Holly noted, if you want to upgrade your personal devices, don’t wait. Look for the best price you can find and buy it right away. Otherwise, prices may go up while you wait.

Last year, CNET found that US adults planned to spend an average of $931 on holiday shopping. This year, shoppers are planning to spend less.

On average, they expect to spend $808 on holiday shopping. That’s $123 less than last year. Some generations plan to spend more, such as millennials, who anticipate an average holiday shopping outlay of $1,074. Boomers will spend around half that amount — $582.

Higher everyday living costs could explain why holiday budgets are lower.“Everything else being more expensive means less left over for gifts,” said Holly. “There’s very little indication that component prices are going to come back down anytime soon, so if you’re hoping for the kinds of prices you saw even two years ago, I would say you’re going to be waiting quite a while.”

Balancing holiday gifts and everyday basics on your usual income can be a lot to handle. Now’s the time to set holiday expectations, including a budget and a list of must-haves, along with more affordable options that still meet your needs.

Then keep checking prices and deals from your trusted retailers and be prepared to buy when you spot good savings. Most importantly, try to avoid using credit cards and buy-now, pay-later plans that can lead to debt. The Federal Reserve’s recent rate hike held rates elevated, which means borrowing costs will remain high and make debt more expensive through higher credit card and loan interest rates.

CNET found that 73% of shoppers plan to buy tech products or services this season, but what most US adults plan to buy and how much they plan to spend may surprise you.

Thirty percent of shoppers plan to purchase toys, and 25% plan to buy kitchen items, such as air fryers and cookware. But shoppers don’t plan to buy as many personal electronics and home entertainment products. Only 20% plan to buy headphones or earbuds, and even fewer plan to buy video games for consoles (18%) or laptops and TVs (11%). More shocking is that only 13% plan to buy phones. We’ve seen prices increase across popular tech devices and brands due to the RAM shortage, which has led to low supply and high demand for memory chips.

Some of the latest releases cost way more than the average $808 most US adults plan to spend. For instance, the $2,000 iPhone Duo alone costs even more than the average $1,704 that millennials plan to spend on tech this holiday season. And less costly phones are still beyond holiday budgets, like the $1,200 iPhone 18 Pro Max, and even the iPhone 18 Pro is $1,200. Trade-in offers and sales can help lower that cost if you’re planning to upgrade, but shop around and compare deals before buying.

Increased prices may make you reconsider whether to stick with your current model or upgrade, but remember, you have options.

“If the current laptop works well enough, upgrading can either be viewed as a luxury purchase for later or shifted to buying used or refurbished models to save extra,” Holly said.

You may also consider a slightly older model of the device you’re looking for. It could still have all of the features you need, but cost less. Another money-saving option is to consider refurbished tech that’s in excellent or good condition from a certified refurbished retailer. You may still notice some price increases due to demand, but it could still cost less than the newest models.

Most US shoppers (84%) expect the holiday shopping season to come with a few hurdles this year. Forty-three percent are concerned about deceptive pricing practices, such as retailers raising original prices before discounting them for a sale. Others are concerned about deals selling out immediately because of low stock or automated buying bots (39%).

But if you’re more worried about fake deals or sales being a money grab by retailers, Holly said that historically, there have been some great sales ahead of the holidays. It’s still best to do your research before buying to make sure you’re getting a deal by comparing retailer prices before and after announced sales and using price tracking tools, like CamelCamelCamel. Heads up that many retailers, like Amazon, have flash sales with specific times of deeper discounts, and you’ll need to act fast, so it’s best to plan your holiday shopping now.

“The best thing anyone can do ahead of a shopping event is prepare,” said Holly. “Find your favorite price tracker tool before the event starts, have a general idea of what you’re looking to buy and be sure to keep an eye out for bigger discounts when you bundle things together.”

CNET commissioned YouGov Plc to conduct the survey. All figures, unless otherwise stated, are from YouGov Plc. The total sample size was 2,615 adults, of whom 1,552 were interested in purchasing consumer tech products or services this winter holiday season. Fieldwork was undertaken Sept. 3-6, 2026. The survey was carried out online. The figures have been weighted and are representative of all US adults (aged 18 and older).

#3078. Your Google AI mode searches can stay private now with ‘temporary threads’ – here’s how

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

With temporary threads, any searches you run in Google’s AI Mode won’t be associated with your account or saved to your chat history.

Most of the major AIs offer a temporary chat or incognito option in which your conversation remains private and vanishes as soon as your chat ends. Now Google has jumped on board this bandwagon with its AI Mode searches.

Also: Google is making it easier to opt out of Gemini AI training

New to Google’s AI Mode is an option known as temporary threads. By choosing this setting, any searches you conduct in AI mode are detached from your own Google account and history. Your temporary searches won’t be affected by your past preferences or chats. They won’t be impacted by any personalization you’ve set up through your account. And they won’t be saved to your chat history. The goal here is to prevent anyone else, including Google, from accessing your conversations in this mode.

This option is currently rolling out around the world in all languages to Google search on both desktop and mobile browsers. You can run a temporary thread on any device and in any browser.

Try this for yourself: Head to the regular Google search page and click the button on the search field for AI Mode. You should then see an icon with a pen hovering over a dotted circle. If you don’t see it, you may have to run a search to get started. On the results page, you should then spot the icon.

Hover over the icon, and the tooltip will say: “Start temporary thread.” Click the icon on the left to start a new thread. Now, any conversation you kick off will be temporary and unconnected to your account. But you don’t have to stick with just plain old text. Select the plus icon to upload an image or file. Select the microphone icon to speak instead of type.

Also: Goodbye, Gemini Gems: How to use Google’s new Skills

Certain limitations are in effect with a temporary thread. Specifically, you can’t do any of the following:

Are these temporary threads truly private? Here’s what Google says:

“Temporary threads will not be saved to your Google account and disappear after 24 hours,” Google said on a support page. “They won’t be used to train Google’s generative AI models, unless you submit feedback or it’s necessary for safety purposes. Google will still collect data and use data that is not associated with your account, including to keep our services working smoothly and safely and to support business operations.”

Google also warns that your browser may still save your history if you visit a website within a temporary thread. Data could still be collected by the sites you visit and the services those sites use, including Google services like Google Analytics.

Also: I asked Gemini Notebook to ‘make me a site’ from my notes

ChatGPT, Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot all offer a temporary chat mode that also promises to keep your chats private and unconnected to your account. Claude and Perplexity provide the same feature but call it incognito mode.

(Disclosure: Ziff Davis, ZDNET’s parent company, filed an April 2025 lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging it infringed Ziff Davis copyrights in training and operating its AI systems.)

Partnerships with Amazon and Ulta reach new shoppers without pulling sales from Bath & Body Works' own stores, a tension investors will want to watch.

10 stocks we like better than Bath & Body Works ›

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 19, 2026, Bath & Body Works (BBWI +3.19%) announced that net sales reached $1.6 billion, exceeding management guidance. The retailer is executing a multiyear strategy to launch new product franchises and expand distribution outside traditional stores. Three things management said stand out.

Management launched new product lines, including Essentials body care for sensitive skin and Everyday Luxuries high-concentration fragrances, to build stand-alone platforms that command higher selling prices. Early repeat purchase rates for these lines are above the company's historical average.

Partnerships with Amazon, an online marketplace, and Ulta, a beauty retailer, give the business access to new shoppers without cannibalizing its owned channels. Management is expanding wholesale distribution to capture incremental demand while protecting its store economics.

The company's Fuel for Growth efficiency initiative, an internal cost-reduction program, is outperforming original expectations. Management is funneling those savings into marketing campaigns and digital capabilities to support long-term top-line growth.

Digital sales are growing again, and management isn't hiding its enthusiasm about the channel's turnaround. The retailer retains structural advantages through its massive store footprint and high-margin product launches, while leadership watches store traffic trends and tariff cost pressures. Management's strategic focus remains centered on scaling successful platforms.

Long-term growth depends on turning early product and marketplace wins into durable, repeatable platforms. Management is driving the organization toward full execution across all key selling channels.

Hyatt is updating its rewards program in 2027, and it means you'll earn Milestone Rewards even sooner than before.

Editor/Content Strategist & Smart Travel Podcast Host

It’s going to be easier to rack up extra benefits if you’re a frequent Hyatt customer in 2027. World of Hyatt announced new Milestone Rewards, the ability to stack awards (such as Free Night Certificates and Suite Upgrade Awards) on a single stay and a simpler 365-day expiration on all awards.

The news expands on the fresh details revealed Nov. 17, 2026, around World of Hyatt’s partnership with Delta SkyMiles, which was first announced in September.

The additions to the Milestone Rewards are designed to give members more choice and personalization, according to Laurie Blair, senior vice president of global marketing and loyalty at Hyatt.

"We’re shaping the future of World of Hyatt around what our members value most. After a year of listening, one thing is clear: members want more distinctive benefits, more freedom to use their awards and the opportunity to choose awards that matter most to them,” Blair said in an email to NerdWallet.

But top-tier Globalist members will soon have to choose between perks that they previously received automatically. Most notably, Globalists will no longer receive free parking on award nights in 2027. Instead, they can choose a Free Parking Award as a Milestone Reward that they can apply to award or paid stays.

The Delta Air Lines and Hyatt partnership will also mainly benefit frequent flyers and hotel guests. With the exception of the limited-time intro promotion, only Delta or Hyatt members with elite status will earn points in both programs. Hyatt elites will have to purchase premium tickets on Delta — not economy — to earn Hyatt points on the flight.

Starting Jan. 1, 2027, World of Hyatt will extend Milestone Rewards to guests who have not yet qualified for the first level of elite status. Southwest Airlines did the same in its recent revamp to give loyal customers a thank you before they’ve reached any level of elite status.

World of Hyatt members will reach the first Milestone Reward at just 10 nights or 20,000 Base Points. Previously, it was 20 nights or 35,000 Base Points.

The reward choices at the first milestone are:

A tier-qualifying night credit, which gets you closer to the next level of elite status.

A $25 FIND Experience credit (Hyatt’s platform for local experiences such as cooking classes).

A $30 spa credit good at Hyatt Inclusive Collection resorts.

The latter two will likely still require you to pay money out of pocket to use them, as the credit will only cover a portion of your bill. For example, the cheapest spa treatment at Secrets Playa Mujeres Golf & Spa Resort in Cancun, Mexico, will still run you $109 (or $79 after the credit).

The Milestone Rewards start to get good at the higher tiers. Starting at 20 nights, you can select from the existing Milestone Rewards, as well as new items. Some of the new options include:

Free parking on award nights is going away as a Globalist tier benefit. In 2027, a Free Parking Award will be an option that Globalists can select at the 60, 70, 80 and 90 nights The parking award can be used on either a qualifying award or paid stay for up to seven nights.

Hyatt said in a call with NerdWallet that roughly 70% of Globalists weren’t using the free parking benefit at all.

Globalists who have earned status in 2026 for 2027 will be grandfathered into the automatic free parking on award stays through their tier expiration date in February 2028.

To use these new awards, the Hyatt booking process is also getting an upgrade. Previously, awards like Suite Upgrade Awards and Free Night Awards couldn’t be redeemed on the same stay. Starting in 2027, members can combine eligible awards on a single reservation, including Suite Upgrade Awards, Guest of Honor Awards and Free Parking Awards.

The new booking system will also make it easier to pay for some nights of a single reservation with awards, points, cash or a combination of points and cash.

Every award earned going forward will also carry a 365-day expiration from the date it’s issued, replacing the patchwork of different validity windows. Previously, Suite Upgrade and Guest of Honor Awards expired at “rest of year plus 14 days,” which was just a tad confusing. Meanwhile, Free Night Awards earned through Milestone Rewards were valid for 180 days from the date of issuance, which was not a lot of time to plan a trip.

The Milestone Rewards kick in next year, but the other big change around the Delta partnership is available now.

Hyatt elite members can earn World of Hyatt Bonus Points on eligible Delta flights (Delta Comfort, Premium Select, First Class and Delta One). Basic Economy or standard Main Cabin fares will earn nothing from this partnership at all.

Discoverist members earn 1 Bonus Point per $2 spent.

Explorist, Globalist and Lifetime Globalist members earn 1 Bonus Point per $1 spent.

Delta Medallion members (Silver through Diamond) can earn 1 Delta mile per $1 spent at participating Hyatt properties, on top of their regular Hyatt points.

Even if you don’t have elite status with either program, it’s still worth linking accounts to take advantage of the upcoming bonus point promotions:

Those who link their accounts and complete a qualifying Hyatt stay from Nov. 17 to Dec. 31, 2026, will earn one bonus Tier-Qualifying Night Credit.

A second bonus point offer runs Jan. 4 through Feb. 15, 2027, for members who take their first Delta flight or Hyatt stay after linking their accounts. Members will earn 1,000 Delta SkyMiles after the Hyatt stay or 1,000 Hyatt points after their first flight in a premium cabin on Delta.

Hyatt and Delta are also holding a sweepstakes through Nov. 23 — no points or miles required to enter — for a free three-night trip for two at Alila Mayakoba in Riviera Maya, Mexico, plus two $1,000 Delta gift cards. Linking your accounts before entering gets you a bonus entry.

If you are interested in dual accrual in 2027, there are some routes to elite status through travel credit cards. Hyatt’s entry-level elite tier comes as a benefit of holding the World of Hyatt Credit Card, but Discoverists earn Hyatt points at half the rate of Explorist and Globalist elites on premium Delta fares.

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

There's something to play whether you're into science fiction, horror or other genres.

Grand Theft Auto 6 might be one of the most anticipated game releases of the year, but not everyone likes the series or is interested in it. But if you want to play something more fantastical, Xbox Game Pass has you covered with High on Life 2, Helo: of Mice and Magic and more soon.

Xbox Game Pass, a CNET Editors’ Choice award winner, offers a wide selection of games you can play on your Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S, Xbox One and PC or mobile device for as little as $10 per month. With a higher-tier Game Pass Ultimate subscription ($23 per month), you can access hundreds of titles, including new ones on release day, each month.

Here’s everything Microsoft is adding to Xbox Game Pass soon.

New to Game Pass Premium. Previously added to Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass.

This sequel to the 2022 first-person shooter High on Life has players once again traveling throughout space and taking down bad guys with the help of an arsenal of talking guns. The game comes from Squanch Games, which was founded by a co-creator of the Rick and Morty series, so expect some raunchy humor and antics.

This prequel to the Outlast series retains the horror of the other games and adds a Cold War-era twist. You’ve been abducted and are subjected to medical and psychological experiments. To survive, you have to fight and evade other test subjects in a massive facility run by the shady Murkoff Corporation.

You’ve seen mice, right? Small, cute creatures that scamper around and are sometimes kept as pets? Well, in this co-op game, you get to see the world through the eyes of one of those critters. You’ll solve puzzles, explore landscapes inspired by Northern Sweden and take in a heartwarming story told via fuzzy friends.

While Microsoft is adding several games to Game Pass, it’s also removing eight others on Nov. 30. So you still have some time to complete your main campaign or any side quests before you’ll have to buy these games separately.

For more, read our Xbox Game Pass review and learn about other titles you can play on the service. You can also check out our recent review of the Xbox Nano Controller.

#3074. I’ve tested countless Linux distros, and Pond is unlike anything I’ve tried – here’s why

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Linux

Feeling adventurous? This Linux distribution is exciting, efficient and totally unique.

Linux is all about choice. From the kernel all the way up to the desktop environment, you get to determine what is used and even how it is used. The staggering number of distributions, desktops, package managers, file managers, and terminal apps provide you with a nearly infinite combination of choices. That choice is and has always been a key aspect of Linux.

Also: My favorite Linux desktop environment for laptops surprised even me

So too is innovation. If there’s one thing that separates Linux from all other operating systems, it’s the willingness to try something different. Linux developers are always pushing the limits of what an operating system is, and this new take on the OS is the epitome of that.

The distribution in question is called Pond. According to the developers, “Pond is an opportunity for us to play with familiar conventions and experiment with new ideas that make a computer more natural and satisfying.”

The developers have achieved something special. Pond takes the standard UI and turns it on its head. Part tiling window manager, part mobile UI, part GNOME, and part something we’ve never before seen, this desktop environment is special. It took me all of five minutes to fall in love with what they’ve created.

Also: The only 4 Linux email clients I recommend

If you’ve ever considered using a tiling window manager, but thought the lack of a mouse made it seem a bit too complicated, Pond is exactly what you want. Here’s how it works:

Pond uses the Niri window manager to arrange windows in columns along an infinite strip from left to right. In multi-monitor setups, each display gets its own strip, so windows never “overflow” from one monitor to the next.

Also: How to install Arch Linux without losing your mind

At the same time, workspaces are dynamic, and there’s always a new workspace automatically created to the right of the farthest-right window. The combination of the Pond sidebar and Niri’s way of handling windows makes this UI truly original.

Pond doesn’t have a traditional desktop menu. Instead, you open the launcher (using the Super+Space key combination), type the name of the app you want to install, and hit Enter when the app name appears on both the display and as an icon in the top portion of the sidebar.

Another thing that sets Pond apart is how you install apps. Yes, you can open a terminal window and install an app using the pacman command, or you can open the launcher, type install, press Enter, and then type the name of the app you want to install. For instance, if you wanted to install LibreOffice, you would type:

Once you hit Enter a second time, the installation will begin. Many apps install via Flatpak, but on the off-chance an app must be installed via the pacman package manager, you’ll be prompted to type your user password before the installation begins.

As I hinted earlier, Pond is based on Arch Linux, which means it’s a rolling-release distribution. One issue that did give me pause was the lack of a GUI update system, which indicates that updates would have to happen in the terminal, like so:

I installed the Shelly GUI frontend, which does have an update component. Personally, I would simply open the terminal window, type sudo pacman -Syu, hit Enter, and let the update run in the background. But if a GUI is your jam, Shelly is what you want.

Also: A super fast distro for anyone ready to move beyond beginner Linux

It would be sweet if the developers allowed updating the system from within the launcher, so it didn’t require opening the terminal first. The Pond launcher does allow running system commands from the launcher, which will then open the terminal window and execute the command. For instance, open the terminal, type a command, hit Enter, and then scroll through the list of available commands that can be run.

Pond ships with kernel 7.3.4-3, so it has outstanding hardware recognition and performance.

You should definitely give Pond a try, especially if you’re adventurous and want to experience something completely different. If, on the other hand, different is not in your stream, then Pond will frustrate you to no end.

Also: Why Nextcloud Office is my new favorite free productivity suite

Pond excited me more than any OS has in a very long time; so much so that I could see this becoming my go-to OS, once it reaches stable release. Until then, I will keep Pond installed on a laptop, keep upgrading, and see what happens next.

Kudos to the Pond OS team for coming up with something truly unique in an already competitive world.

#3073. Northern Tech (NTIC) Q4 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Sales hit records, but raw material costs weighed on profits.

By Motley Fool Transcribing – Nov 19, 2026 at 1:54PM EST

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Northern Technologies (NTIC +0.13%) reported record fiscal 2026 consolidated revenue of $95,981,956, although management indicated that profitability did not keep pace with top-line growth. The company appointed Gautam Ramdas as Chief Executive Officer in Sept. 2026, who has prioritized improving operating profitability and cash flow as central objectives for the upcoming fiscal year. Management reported that while segments like ZERUST industrial and oil and gas achieved record annual sales, margins were compressed by volatile raw material costs and a shift in product mix. To address these challenges, the company is focusing on global coordination of research and development, the introduction of higher-margin adjacent products, and the restructuring of joint venture payment models to accelerate cash repatriation.

Operator: Good day, and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the Northern Technologies International Corporation Fourth Quarter 26 Earnings Conference Call. I would now like to hand the conference over to Gautam Ramdas, President and Chief Executive Officer.

Gautam Ramdas: Good morning. I am Gautam Ramdas, NTIC CEO. And I am here with Matthew Wolsfeld, NTIC CFO. Please note that a press release regarding our fourth quarter and full year fiscal 26 financial results was issued earlier this morning, and is available at ntic.com. During today's call, we will review various key aspects of our fiscal 26 fourth quarter and full year financial results provide a brief business update, and then conclude with a question and answer session. Please note that when we discuss year over year performance, are referring to the fourth quarter and full year of our fiscal 26 in comparison to the fourth quarter and full year of our fiscal 25.

Before reviewing our results, I would like to take a few minutes to introduce myself share some observations from my first month as CEO, and discuss the priorities guiding our approach to the business. I assume the CEO role in September, succeeding Patrick Lynch, who continues to serve NTIC as chairman of our board. I want to thank Patrick for his leadership and the tremendous contributions he has made in building NTIC into the global company it is today. I have been with NTIC for more than 20 years. Most recently leading our ZERUST Integrity Solutions business including the expansion of our presence in the global oil and gas industry.

My background combines engineering, management consulting, international business development, and working directly with customers to solve complex technical challenges. Over the years, I have worked closely with our employees, joint venture partners, and most importantly, customers across many of our markets. This experience has given me a strong appreciation for MTXC's capabilities, the value we deliver to our customers, and the opportunities that exist to drive our success in the future. Since September, I have spent considerable time engaging with our teams, reviewing our operations, meeting some key customers, engaging with our joint ventures, and evaluating the opportunities and challenges across our businesses.

These discussions have reinforced my confidence in NTIC's foundation and highlight the global opportunities to further connect our technical capabilities, customer relationships, and global resources. We have proprietary technologies decades of corrosion prevention experience, established customer relationships, and a global presence spanning more than 65 countries. Our business is diversified across products, customers, industries, and geographies, providing us with multiple avenues for growth. NTIC does not simply sell products. Our technical teams work directly with customers to understand their challenges and develop engineered solutions that protect critical assets improve operating efficiency, and reduce cost. That combination of technical knowledge, local market presence, and close customer relationships is a critical differentiator for NTIC. I believe we can further leverage these advantages.

Our markets are constantly evolving, Industrial demand shifts between regions. Customers face increasingly complex technical challenges. Infrastructure is aging, environmental and regulatory requirements are changing. While NTI sees diversity across markets, products, customers, and geographies, supports a differentiated platform we can additionally pursue new strategies identifying opportunities developing solutions, and bringing them to market. In our ZERUST industrial business, we have a well established position in corrosion prevention, supported by long standing relationships with major industrial customers around world. This is a strong business that provides an important foundation for our company. At the same time, we see opportunities to expand into adjacent applications and increase our market penetrations in markets where we already have an established presence.

Earlier this year, we launched a new range of products for hydrostatic testing, primarily in the oil and gas sector, and we are now starting to get some of our industrial clients in trials using this product. This leverages our existing Salesforce and distribution channels both our own and those that are joint ventures. In ZERUST Oil and Gas, we have expanded our focus beyond storage tanks and pipelines to include preservation of critical infrastructure like floating production, storage, offloading vessels or FPSOs. As well as working with shipyards, fabricators, and OEMs within the supply chain. Having worked extensively in this business, I know firsthand the technical advantages of our solutions, and the value they can provide to our customers.

And we launched ZERUST Integrity Solutions also known as ZIS, to combine our expertise in corrosion mitigation along with our traditional product suite to address the corrosion aspect of asset integrity engagements. Our recent successes in Brazil and The Middle East point to the fact that ZERUST technologies can help operators protect critical infrastructure extend asset life, and reduce long term maintenance costs. This is also highly technical and regulated market where qualification, product validation, and adoption can take time. In certain cases, the process can span several years. While that creates longer sales cycles, it also provides meaningful barriers to entry and potential for durable long term customer relationships once our solutions are adopted.

We have invested in expanding our ZIS approach particularly in international markets, and are pursuing opportunities involving storage tanks pipelines, and new sectors with critical infrastructure like data centers, carbon capture facilities, petrochemical facilities, shipyards, etcetera. Our focus now is on converting these opportunities into sustained revenue growth while leveraging the investments we have made to our oil and gas platform over the past 2 years. Turning to Natur-Tec, I believe the long term opportunity for sustainable and compostable materials remains attractive. Although market conditions and the pace of adoption vary significantly by geography and application. As the market evolves, we intend to remain focused on areas where our technical expertise provides meaningful differentiation.

This includes developing specialized formulations and products that meet increasingly demanding performance requirements while also remaining competitive on price in more commoditized applications. Our ability to work closely with customers understand their specific requirements, and engineer solutions to meet those needs is an important competitive advantage. We intend to leverage that expertise as we pursue new applications and opportunities across global markets. Turning to our fiscal 26 performance. We finished the year with record sales of $96 million, an increase of nearly 14% compared to fiscal 25. Driven by growth across ZERUST industrial, ZERUST oil and gas, and nature tech. Fourth quarter sales increased nearly 19% to a quarterly record of $20.5 million.

Reflecting strong demand in ZERUST industrial Natur Tec products, partially offset by lower ZERUST oil and gas sales. For the fiscal year, ZERUST industrial sales increased 13% to $62.5 million driven by continued demand for our corrosion prevention solutions in North America, and China, and, to a lesser extent, India. Fourth quarter ZERUST industrial sales grew 24%, We are encouraged by the strength of this business and the opportunities to expand into adjacent applications and deepen our presence in markets where we are already established. For fiscal 26, ZERUST oil and gas sales increased 33% to a record $9.8 million, reflecting glow. Growing customer adoption and the investments we have made to expand our global sales and technical capabilities.

During the year, we experienced higher oil and gas sales in The Middle East Brazil, and North America from both new and existing customers. Recent investments in our client-facing teams have given us greater depth in the domain expertise of corrosion as part of larger client asset integrity programs and that has improved our sales pipeline. We are focused on driving further growth under the ZIS initiatives in fiscal 27. However, sales in both oil and gas and new sectors can be volatile from quarter to quarter, given the size and timing of individual orders. An ongoing cause of concern is the current conflict in The Middle East, in which several of our clients have been impacted.

And there is potential for a slowdown until the situation stabilizes. Natur-Tec, our bioplastics division, achieved record sales for both full year and fourth quarter increasing 9% and 23%, respectively. This growth reflects continued demand for our compostable materials, and expanding opportunities across global markets. In North America, we are advancing compostable food packaging solutions through the International Fresh Produce Association's packaging innovation program. In India, our collaboration with Bayer to develop biodegradable and compostable seedling cups represents another promising application for our technology. Combined, these initiatives reflect our focus on leveraging our technical expertise to develop differentiated higher value solutions across a growing range of applications.

Turning to our global joint ventures, Fiscal 26 sales increased nearly 10% to $100 million. Reflecting continued demand across our international markets. Our joint venture partners have been instrumental in establishing NTIC's global presence and remain a critical component of our business model. Their local market knowledge and long standing customer relationships enable us to serve customers around the world while maintaining a capital efficient operating structure. As we look ahead, I see opportunities to strengthen collaboration with our joint venture partners share best practices, and further leverage our global network to pursue additional growth opportunities. These results demonstrate the strength of our business the demand for our solutions across global markets.

While we are pleased with our growth and record slate levels, we recognize that our profitability has not kept pace. Higher input costs, competitive pricing pressures, change in product mix, and investments to support our growth are weighed on margins and earnings. We intend to next focus on converting our revenue growth into improved operating profitability and cash flow. This will be a central priority for our leadership team over the near term. We have spent years building our global infrastructure, developing proprietary tech technologies, and expanding our commercial capabilities. As we look ahead, our focus is on generating additional revenues from those investments.

We intend to accomplish this by strategically allocating resources prioritizing opportunities where we can deliver the greatest value to customers, increasing efficiency across our operations. Our global footprint is an important competitive advantage and I intend to ensure that our teams are working together effectively sharing knowledge and best practices, taking full advantage of the capabilities we have developed. I am fortunate to have a talented and experienced team including Brian Haglund, who was recently promoted to chief operating officer. Brian and I share a commitment to operational excellence, disciplined and continuing to build a scalable and profitable business. We also recognize that these strategic initiatives will take time.

We operate in diverse markets, and we cannot control their economic, geopolitical, or regulatory environments. But we can control how effectively we respond, where we focus our efforts, and how efficiently we operate. As we enter fiscal 27, I am optimistic about NTIC's future. We have a strong foundation, diversified global business, differentiated technologies, and meaningful opportunities to expand our presence in both existing and new markets. Our objective is not simply to grow NTIC, but to build a stronger, more focused, and more profitable company. 1 that fully leverages its technology, its people, its global reach to deliver sustainable growth and create long term shareholder value.

I look forward to keeping you updated on our progress So with this overview, let me now turn the call over to Matthew Wolsfeld to summarize our financial results for the fourth quarter and full fiscal year 2026.

Matthew Wolsfeld: Thanks, Gautam. Before reviewing our financial results, I would like to take the moment to welcome Gautam to his new role as President and CEO. I have had the pleasure of working closely with Gautam for many years, and have seen firsthand his deep technical expertise, understanding of our business, and commitment to our customers. I am excited about the perspective and leadership he brings to this role and look forward to working together as we build on NTIC's strong foundation and pursue the opportunities ahead. Now turning to our fourth quarter and full year fiscal 26 financial results.

Compared to the prior fiscal year period NTIC's consolidated net sales increased 13.9% in fiscal 26 and increased 18.6% in the fiscal 26 fourth quarter. The third consecutive quarter of year over year double digit growth. Sales across our joint ventures increased 4% in the fourth quarter. Joint venture operating income in the fourth quarter decreased 27.7% compared to the prior fiscal year period. Primarily due to lower fees for services provided by joint ventures, following the modification of fees at our German and French joint ventures and lower profitability at our German joint venture. For fiscal 26, sales across our global joint ventures increased 9.7% while joint venture operating income decreased 1.3% compared to the prior fiscal period.

Gross profit as a percentage of net sales was 35.0%, during the 3 months ended August 31, 2026. Compared to 37.9% during the prior fiscal year period. Gross profit as a percentage of net sales was 35.0% for the fiscal year ended August 31, 2026, compared to 37.6% for the prior fiscal year. The fiscal year over year decrease in gross margin was primarily due to higher raw material costs including resin and solvents, were only partially recovered through price increases. Lower selling prices on certain Natur Tec products, and a lower margin sales mix.

Total operating expenses for fiscal 20 fourth quarter increased 6.4% to $10.3 million primarily due to strategic investments in NTIC's oil and gas marketing and sales efforts. Including personnel expenses and the corresponding benefits. As well as the increased travel and professional fees. Operating expenses as a percentage of fourth quarter sales were 39.0% compared to 43.5% for the prior fiscal year period. Continue to expect quarterly sales to grow faster than operating expenses, as we continue to leverage recent investments and upgrades across our global operations. For fiscal 26, operating expenses as a percentage of net sales were 41.4% compared to 44.7% for the prior fiscal year. Income before income tax expense was $1.8 million for fiscal 26.

Compared to $3.0 million last year. NTIC recognized $1.1 million in other income during the 12 months ended August 31, 2025 due to the receipt of a cash ERC payment. No other income was recognized during the 12 months ended August 31, 2026. NTIC's effective income tax rate increased to 86.3% for fiscal 26, from 67.5% in the prior fiscal year. The increase primarily reflects lower pretax income relative to income taxes incurred at NTIC's profitable foreign subsidiaries which are taxed at statutory rates that exceed The US rate in certain jurisdictions. Notably Brazil and India, and bear withholding taxes and royalty and dividend payments.

NTSC also recorded no income tax benefit in its US pretax loss as a full valuation allowance is maintained against its US deferred tax assets. These items were partially offset by nontaxable equity income from NTI International Joint Ventures and research and development credits. As a result, NTIC's effective tax rate was unusually high and volatile for fiscal 26. Although we expect the effective tax rate to normalize in future periods when additional profits are recognized in our North American operations, it is possible that rates remain volatile due to a variety of factors. NTSC reported a net loss of $6.64 million or $0.07 per diluted share for the fiscal 26 fourth quarter.

Compared to a net loss of $1.1 million $0.12 per diluted share for the fiscal 25 fourth quarter. For the full year, NTIC reported a net loss of $703,000 or $0.07 per diluted share. Compared to net income of $18,000 or $0.00 per diluted share for the fiscal 25 full year. For the fiscal 26 fourth quarter, NTIC's non GAAP adjusted net loss was $537,000 or $0.06 per diluted share compared to a non GAAP adjusted net loss of $607,000 or $0.06 per diluted share for fiscal 25 fourth quarter.

For fiscal 26, non GAAP adjusted net loss was $280,000 or $0.03 per diluted share compared to a non GAAP adjusted loss of $12,000 or $0.00 per diluted share for fiscal 25. A reconciliation of GAAP to non GAAP financial measures is available on our fourth quarter and full year 2026 earnings press release that was issued this morning. As of August 31, 2026, working capital was $20.1 million including $7.0 million in cash and cash equivalents. Compared to $20.4 million including $7.3 million in cash and cash equivalents as of August 31, 2025. As of August 31, 2026, we had an outstanding revolving line of credit and current portion of term loan balance of $14.2 million.

Compared to $12.2 million as of August 31, 2025. This included $11.1 million in borrowings under our revolving line of credit. Compared to $9.3 million as of August 31, 2025. Reducing debt through positive operating cash flow and improving working capital efficiencies is a strategic near term focus. During the third quarter of fiscal 26, we committed to a plan to sell our Beechwood, Ohio facility, which has historically been used by our ZERUST segment. As a result, we are classifying the carrying value of the property of $856,000 from property, plant, and equipment net to assets held for sale for the consolidated balance sheet as of August 31, 2026.

Following the termination of the original purchase agreement in September, we entered into a new definitive agreement with a different unrelated buyer in early November to sell the property for $1.1 million in cash. We currently expect the transaction to close during the second quarter of fiscal 27 subject to customary closing conditions. However, there can be no assurances that the sale will be completed on the terms described or at all. On August 31, 2026, the company had $30.7 million of investment in joint ventures. Of which 58.8% or $8.1 million was in cash while the remaining balance primarily invested in other working capital.

To conclude, fiscal 26 was a year of record consolidated sales, reflecting continued demand for our solutions and growth across all 3 of our businesses. While we are encouraged by our sales performance, we recognize the need to translate that growth into stronger profitability and cash flow. As Gautam discussed, we believe NTIC has a strong foundation supported by our proprietary technologies, established global infrastructure, and long standing customer relationships. Our focus as we enter fiscal 27 is on leveraging these strengths. Maintaining operating discipline, and improving financial performance while pursuing the growth opportunities ahead. With this overview, Gautam and I are happy to take your questions.

#3072. Amid Anthropic’s IPO, Google, Microsoft and OpenAI Drop New AI Models

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

With the focus on Nvidia and Anthropic, several new models were released by OpenAI and Microsoft.

It’s been a wild week for the AI industry — and it’s only Thursday. Aside from outages, cheating scandals and Anthropic’s pending IPO, there are several new models available now. Google dropped Gemini 4 Neon, Microsoft dropped seven new versions of its MAI models at its Ignite conference, and OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, the next step forward for its flagship models.

Next, Microsoft: At its Ignite developer conference on Tuesday, Microsoft introduced seven new AI models. They include MAI Cyber 2 Flash, MAI Code 2, MAI Image 2.7 and Dragon Copilot Transcribe — models meant to help with tasks in cybersecurity, coding, image generation and transcription.

It’s clear from Microsoft’s marketing that it is aiming to position its new tech as a cheaper alternative to OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s leading models, with many of these significantly cheaper to run at the enterprise level. That, plus its new licensed weight program, which lets companies customize the new AI models for their purposes, highlights how Microsoft is continuing to pitch its AI tech to the workplace.

While these new models might be useful for AI power users, they are far from most of the AI industry’s mind this week. During Tuesday’s earnings call, new interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress tried to assure investors that everything was “business as usual” after weeks of turmoil inside the company rocked the global economy. Nvidia cofounder and now-former CEO Jensen Huang’s multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence, threw the company into chaos and have attracted the attention of the Securities and Exchange Commission and both chambers of Congress, where Huang has agreed to testify.

And then there’s Anthropic. The Claude maker is becoming a public company this week, with the possible biggest-ever IPO. Anthropic had an opening price of $83 per share, valuing it at $1.5 trillion — narrowly surpassing the valuation of Elon Musk’s mega-conglomerate, SpaceX, at its record-setting IPO earlier this year (now with SpaceXSI, because President Donald Trump said so).

The Nvidia scandal caused a drastic 14% dip in its stock price during its first week and wiped out $1 trillion in the company’s value, but Anthropic investors don’t seem to be worried. At least, not publicly.

If nothing else, Anthropic’s IPO and the new models from Google, OpenAI and Microsoft are stark reminders that the tech industry is nowhere near ready to slow down on AI. Even as financial, environmental and legal concerns mount — and arguably hit a fever pitch during the midterm elections — Big Tech is plowing ahead with generative AI.

#3071. Meta Muse booked an Airbnb without permission – and that’s not the worst of it

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Also: Don’t use Muse? Meta’s AI agent can still access your private messages

According to a Reuters investigation, Meta employees testing Muse said the agent messaged them about topics they hadn’t asked it about, including career advice, a follow-up on a request for childcare, products they hadn’t purchased, and, crucially, bank account balances they didn’t recognize.

These incidents “prompted unnerved employees to raise concerns it could be mixing up conversations between different accounts and exposing users’ private data,” Reuters said.

Reuters said “an employee told colleagues his Muse had randomly added an extra message to its regular chats about fishing-related weather and tide information, saying: ‘BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2,722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5,899.57.'” In another instance, Muse booked a non-refundable Airbnb for an employee who hadn’t instructed it to.

Muse notified another employee, who was using the agent on her personal phone, about a message she’d received on Signal, though she said she hadn’t given the agent access to the encrypted messaging app.

Reuters and the AI Now Institute determined, through testing on an Android phone and a Mac, that Muse used “permissions granted during the bot’s initial setup to pull in the message text, leveraging those authorizations in ways a user might not anticipate.” Because Muse is set up with automatic access to Android push notifications, it didn’t need explicit app access to read messages.

The tests did not work on an iPhone, suggesting better protections against Muse’s prying.

Similarly, in September, a user reported Muse had shared his address with a Facebook Marketplace buyer before checking with him. The incident was ultimately a misunderstanding between the terms the user thought he’d consented to and how much access he was actually handing over, which exemplifies that Meta and the user may have explicitly different definitions of access, and that Muse can take advantage of that grey area.

Meta told Reuters these incidents were either isolated or the result of hallucinations, though Reuters could not confirm that.

Also: How to keep your chatbot conversations as private as possible

Reuters’ findings may provide an opportunity for Google’s agentic offering, now called Tasks (formerly Spark), which it made free (with usage limits, like Muse) this week.

TL;DR: Mortgage rates eased today, but borrowing costs are still expensive for many homebuyers.

Mortgage rates are lower today, but recent averages above 7% are still eating into buyers’ budgets.

The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.13% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 21 basis points lower than yesterday and 13 basis points higher than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.)

Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context:

» Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders

Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

On Friday, the Bureau of Labor Statistics released the Producer Price Index for October, which tracks the change in prices that U.S. producers are able to get for their products. This is one way to measure inflation on the market end, rather than the consumer end.

The results were mixed. While prices didn’t rise quite as high as economists anticipated month-over-month (0.3% vs. 0.4%), year-over-year price growth did reach 6.5% — the largest increase in four years. This points to even higher costs for consumers coming in the near future.

Investors are convinced that the Federal Reserve will raise overnight borrowing rates again in December to pull inflation down. And higher overnight borrowing rates — called the federal funds rate, which is what banks pay to fund products like mortgages — usually lead to higher mortgage rates.

» MORE: How the Federal Reserve affects mortgage rates

Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you plan to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.63% or higher.

Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

» Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders

There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

If the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

NerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a new home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

If you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.
